papers.title: Sharp modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality for matrix-valued functions on spheres
papers.abstract: We prove that for every smooth positive definite matrix-valued function $g$ on the unit sphere $S^d$, \[ \int_{S^d}\tr(g(\log g-\log\E g))\dd \le\dfrac1{2d}\int_{S^d}\tr((\Delta g)\log g)\dd. \] Here $\mu$ is normalized area measure, $\E g$ is the spherical mean, and $\Delta$ is the positive spherical Laplacian. This complete modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality extends Beckner's sharp logarithmic Sobolev inequality, in its modified form, to matrix-valued functions independent of the matrix size. We show that both entropy and Fisher information decay exponentially under the heat flow with optimal exponent $2d$, whose proof combines the Bochner identity with a $4$th-tensor estimate in the matrix-valued setting.

papers.title: Michelson and Logarithmic Operator Contrasts Spectral Geometry, Tracial Extensions, and Random Products
papers.abstract: The Michelson contrast of a positive invertible operator is a bounded coordinate for its condition number. Its logarithmic lift, $\operatorname{OLC}(A)=\frac12\log(\|A\|\|A^{-1}\|)$, connects spectral spread with projective Thompson geometry. This preprint collects the Novikov--Nikolaeva series and the associated single-author extensions by Novikov into one treatment. We develop the equality criterion for product subadditivity, its dimension and Jordan-rank thresholds, quantum-state examples, and contrasts associated with unitarily invariant norms. The latter have a sharp additive defect, while the full Schatten family records a logarithmic spectral profile up to homometry. Tracial extensions give characterisations of traces, dimension-sensitive defects, and spectral-edge asymptotics. Unbounded operators are described through critical exponents and finite sections. Tensor, matrix and free independence lead to distinct growth laws for products. Finally, symmetric cones provide a setting for the equality criterion, Lorentz boosts, and Jordan products. Classical ingredients are distinguished from the refinements developed in the series; conjectural asymptotic statements remain explicitly labelled.

papers.title: Actions of quantum groups: the standard implementation and relatively invariant weights
papers.abstract: We establish a characterisation of the standard implementation for actions of locally compact quantum groups on von Neumann algebras, extending results of Daws-Skalski-Viselter and Haagerup. As a consequence, we prove that taking the standard implementation respects morphisms of quantum groups. We also prove that several natural conditions expressing relative $\rho$-invariance for n.s.f. weights are equivalent.

papers.title: Obstructions to Hadamard Deformations of Fourier Matrices
papers.abstract: We study deformations of the Fourier spin model commuting square in the space of commuting squares, or equivalently deformations of the matrix $\sqrt nF_n$, where $F_n$ denotes the Fourier matrix, by complex Hadamard matrices. If $n$ is neither a prime power nor twice a prime, we show that there exist unit vectors in the enveloping tangent space that cannot be realized as directions of convergence of sequential deformations. Consequently, the derivative of any differentiable Hadamard family through $\sqrt nF_n$ has rank strictly smaller than the dimension of the enveloping tangent space at $\sqrt nF_n$ (i.e., the defect of $F_n$). This is particularly surprising because for every $n$ there exist enough one-parameter analytic families to provide a basis of directions in the enveloping tangent space. We obtain cubic obstructions when $n$ has at least three distinct prime divisors, quartic obstructions when it has exactly two and a repeated factor, and quintic obstructions when it is the product of two distinct odd primes. These results extend our order $30$ result from \cite{HN}.

papers.title: The Bessis Moussa Villani conjecture in finite von Neumann algebras
papers.abstract: We prove the Bessis--Moussa--Villani conjecture, which is known for matrix algebras, for bounded operators in a finite von Neumann algebra with a faithful normal tracial state. Following the approach of Heinavaara, for a pair of positive operators, we construct a tracial joint spectral measure on the punctured plane whose moments are the traces of symmetrized words. We construct a scalar measure by holomorphic spectral selection and a Lyapunov identity. An integral identity for its moments then gives positivity of two coordinate-weighted distributions. From these we obtain the planar measure and the Laplace representation of the trace exponential.

papers.title: The Operator Systems of Hankel Matrices and Complex Polynomials
papers.abstract: Using polynomial matrix spectral factorization, we establish a complete order duality between $(n+1)\times(n+1)$ Hankel matrices and complex polynomials of degree at most $2n$ on the real line. The projection construction and trace pairing identify $e_n(t)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}t^{2j}$ as the polynomial order unit corresponding to the restriction of the matrix trace. The Cayley transform relates these matrix orders to Toeplitz matrices and truncated trigonometric polynomials, but for $n\geq 2$ the polynomial systems with units $e_n$ and $(1+t^2)^n$ are not unital order isomorphic. We establish polynomial minimality and Hankel maximality, and characterize positivity of $C^*$-algebra-valued block Hankel matrices through completely positive maps on the polynomial operator system. An augmented Vandermonde decomposition describes polynomial states as trace-one positive Hankel matrices, with extreme states given by normalized evaluations and the leading-coefficient functional at infinity.

papers.title: Quantum Born Geometries from Modular Quantization
papers.abstract: A structural link between quantization and "thermal-doubled" non-commutative Born geometry (with its split-quaternionic structure) is uncovered via Tomita-Takesaki first-quantized modular theory for complexified and polarized ortho-symplectic spaces. Implications for the modular algebraic quantum gravity program (arXiv:1007.4094) hint at further deep modifications of the notions of space and geometry (thermal quantum space-time hypothesis) waiting to be further explored. Speculative suggestions in the direction of A.Sakharov and L.Boyle-K.Finn-N.Turok CPT-mirror cosmologies will be mentioned, among several others. The present work is based on the manuscript "Modular Quantization and Non-commutative Space-time" (now on alphaXiv) that has been shared, with a selected number of researchers, since end of April 2026.

papers.title: The Infinitesimal Covariant Stone-von Neumann Theorem
papers.abstract: In a previous paper, the authors established the Covariant Stone-von Neumann Theorem, which generalizes the Stone-von Neumann Theorem in quantum mechanics and yields a classification of all unitary Heisenberg representations of an abelian elementary $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical system up to unitary equivalence. In this sequel to that paper, we establish an infinitesimal version of the Covariant Stone-von Neumann Theorem in the setting of real elementary $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical systems. Firstly, we generalize Stone's Theorem to secure a one-to-one correspondence between the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary groups and the regular self-adjoint densely defined operators on a Hilbert $ C^{\ast} $-module. Secondly, we define the infinitesimal Heisenberg representations and the infinitesimal Schr\"{o}dinger representation of a real $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical system. Thirdly, we construct a one-to-one correspondence between the unitary Heisenberg representation and the infinitesimal Heisenberg representations of a real $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical system, providing a rigorous two-way passage--which we call ``Heisenberg differentiability-integrability''--between the global unitary formulation of Heisenberg covariance and its infinitesimal formulation in terms of regular self-adjoint densely defined operators. This allows us to prove the Infinitesimal Covariant Stone-von Neumann Theorem: For a real elementary $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical system, every infinitesimal Heisenberg representation is a direct sum of copies of the infinitesimal Schr\"{o}dinger representation. Lastly, we obtain explicit descriptions of the position and momentum operators for a real $ C^{\ast} $-dynamical system and construct a natural common invariant core of analytic vectors for them. All requisite technical domain and integrability issues are fully accounted for.

papers.title: C*-algebras constructed using acyclic groups
papers.abstract: We show that the free group on countably many generators is not $C^\ast$-superrigid. Furthermore, we realize each of $O_{\infty}$ and the Jiang-Su algebra as a crossed product of a commutative $C^\ast$-algebra. Finally, we construct non-trivial, outer actions on classifiable $C^\ast$-algebras whose crossed products exhaust all classifiable $C^\ast$-algebras. The common theme in the proofs is the use of torsion-free, acyclic groups.

papers.title: The metric theory of tracial matrix algebras does not converge
papers.abstract: We show that the theories of tracial matrix algebras and metric unitary groups do not converge with the dimension. In the main argument, we recover the canonical diagonal using spectral gap and internality. Uniform definability of the diagonal and its normalizer then transfers the distinct theories of universal sofic groups to matrix ultraproducts. The same methods show that isomorphisms preserve every internal subalgebra and give fixed finite distance formulas over six unitaries. Finally, we construct an explicit continuum family of matrix ultraproducts with distinct theories and trivial first-order fundamental groups.

papers.title: Cantor correlations II. Synchronicity and bisynchronicity
papers.abstract: We study synchronous and bisynchronous no-signalling correlations, defined over Cantor topological spaces, from the perspectives of both continuous variable quantum information and operator algebra theories. We focus on strategies, satisfying a natural no-signalling condition across the Cantor space levels, called graded, identifying a universal C*-algebra, whose tracial states of different types characterise synchronous correlations of respective types. The universal C*-algebra for bisynchronous graded correlations is shown to coincide with the C*-algebra of a projective limit of free wreath products of quantum permutation groups, introduced by Bhowmick, Goswami and Skalski, and a type description, analogous to the one in the synchronous case, is provided. Extending results in the finite case, we show that bisynchronous graded correlations canonically give rise to factorisable maps on type I factors, defined via Cantor permutation matrices. We examine non-local games over Cantor topological spaces, with inputs/outputs that are finite words of equal length, define corresponding game algebras, and characterise the perfect strategies of the games via the respective game algebras. In the case of the Cantor graph isomorphism game, we provide equivalent descriptions of the existence of perfect strategies of quantum commuting type, in terms of bigalois correspondences, factorisable maps, Cantor permutation intertwiners and game algebra non-triviality. Our results supply a quantum information interpretation of a notion of a quantum isomorphism of locally finite graphs, introduced by Rollier and Vaes, canonically arising from Cantor graphs.

papers.title: Annihilating ideals and Agler--McCarthy spectral varieties in the bidisc
papers.abstract: The closed unit bidisc $\overline{\mathbb{D}^2}$ is known to be a spectral set for any pair $(T_1,T_2)$ of commuting contractions. When each $T_i$ is pure and has finite defect, the pair admits a much smaller spectral set: the closure of a distinguished variety $V\subset \mathbb{D}^2$. We exhibit conditions on $(T_1,T_2)$ that guarantee that no proper closed subset of $\overline{V}$ can be a spectral set. In addition, we examine the relationship between $V$ and the annihilating ideal $Ann(T_1,T_2)$ in $H^\infty(\mathbb{D}^2)$. While $V$ is typically strictly larger than the zero set of $Ann(T_1,T_2)$, we isolate a natural constrained co-extension $(S_1,S_2)$ of $(T_1,T_2)$ whose Taylor spectrum is contained in $V$ and is closely linked to the so-called support of $Ann(T_1,T_2)$. We also find simple conditions on $Ann(T_1)$ detecting whether $Ann(T_1,T_2)$ is the ideal of functions vanishing on the joint point spectrum of $(S_1^*,S_2^*)$.

papers.title: A finitely generated Linear group without property (T) that is neither inner amenable nor properly proximal
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit finitely generated ICC subgroup of $\operatorname{GL}_4(\mathbb{F}_2(t))$ that is neither inner amenable nor properly proximal and does not have Kazhdan's property (T). The group is obtained by adjoining a scalar dilation to Caprace's example. In particular, this has resolved a question due to Boutonnet, Ioana, and Peterson in negative.

papers.title: The Dynamical Radius of Comparison for C*-Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: We introduce a dynamical version $\operatorname{rc} (A, \alpha)$ of the radius of comparison $\operatorname{rc} (A)$ of a unital C*-algebra, based on the dynamical Cuntz semigroup. We also give an intrinsic ordered semigroup definition, which agrees with $\operatorname{rc} (A, \alpha)$ when $A$ is residually stably finite, and is lower semicontinuous for equivariant direct limits with injective unital maps. We construct actions $\alpha$ of $G = \mathbb{Z} / 2 \mathbb{Z}$ on simple unital AH~algebras for which $\operatorname{rc} (A, \alpha)$ lies strictly between $\operatorname{rc} (A)$ and $\operatorname{rc} (A) / \operatorname{card} (G)$, and actions $\alpha$ of a finite group $G$ on unital C*-algebras for which $\operatorname{rc} (A, \alpha)$ lies strictly between $\operatorname{rc} (A)$ and $\operatorname{rc} (C^* (G, A, \alpha))$. For a minimal action of a countable discrete group $G$ on a zero dimensional compact metrizable space $X$, and with $\alpha$ being the corresponding action on $C (X)$, we prove that $\operatorname{rc} (C (X), \alpha) = 0$ if and only if the action on~$X$ has dynamical comparison as defined by Kerr. For finite group actions on simple unital stably finite C*-algebras, assuming the weak tracial Rokhlin property, we get $\operatorname{rc} (A, \alpha) \leq \operatorname{rc} (A) / \operatorname{card} (G)$, and assuming weak tracial strict approximate innerness, we get $\operatorname{rc} (A, \alpha) = \operatorname{rc} (A)$.
